chapter: Family and growing up in Manhattan
title: Stride piano as New York piano; Willie the Lion
summary: Father's friends played stride piano at the house. Procope names Fats Waller, Willie the Lion and James P. Johnson and says he likes the Lion's delicate style best.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: whole lot of friends of my father's, they'd come in the house and jump right on the piano and start playing the piano, you know. Like what they call stride piano. Stride piano's New York piano.
Stride piano is New York piano. I never heard it anywhere else but New York.
That's right. That's what they always say.

Fats Waller, Willy "the Lion", James B. [P.] Johnson, right on down the line. Corky -- there used to be a whole lot who never got much publicity, but a whole lot of them. They played stride piano. That's New York piano.
They always refer to James A. Johnson as the father of stride piano. Was he really the first? Weren't there others?

No. You know they put these names on people. You can't say who is who or what is what, way back to Scott Joplin. What the hell, I mean, you know, all these guys, they played, one copied from the other and the other copied from -- even now you have Fats Waller on a record and you're not sure it's Fats, you know. You say, "Yeah, that's Fats," and then you had Jimmy Johnson, you know. You know, playing about along the same lines. But out of all those piano players, you know, I like Willy "the Lion's" style. You know, he plays that delicate
sort of (Imitating piano). You know, that style. He plays a lot of things. Plus, he can -- look here, Willis "the Lion" plays "Carolina Shout," man, that's the classic all time great, you know. Yeah.
